goal.one_sentence_promise: A continuous locally generated 3D mountain-bike descent with a helmeted rider, physical bicycle geometry and native 24 fps camera and subject animation.
goal.ending_takeaway: Speed is a sequence of controlled choices.

story.setup: A solitary rider enters a high forest trail.
story.escalation: The rider accelerates through trees and over rocky singletrack.
story.turn: The forest opens onto exposed ground with airborne moments.
story.resolution: The trail returns to forest, then the camera rises to leave the rider in the landscape.

reference_decomposition.reference: General sports cinematography grammar; no source footage used
transferable_rules: Establish geography then move close to the bike
Alternate grounded camera and airborne reveal
Keep the same rider and route

visual_grammar.style: Original rendered 3D realism study; physically connected rider and bike; textured mountain terrain; atmospheric perspective
visual_grammar.lighting: Single warm directional key, cool fill, distance haze
depth_rules: Foreground stones, moving rider, forest and mountain backgrounds
typography_rules: One opening title and short ending credit; no debug overlays
texture_rules: CC0 Poly Haven ground materials; authored geometry

effects: locally synthesized tire gravel and jump landing pulses
silence_rules: Short end fade only; no false silence promise
sync_rules: Jump sound events derive from the same world route and time function as picture

shots.visible_event: The same orange-jacketed rider advances along a connected mountain singletrack, viewed in aerial.
shots.subject_motion: Wheels rotate from traveled distance; early pedaling becomes technical coasting; bent limbs stay attached to controls; lean follows route curvature.
shots.environment_motion: World-fixed trees and rocks create depth-dependent parallax.
shots.palette: ochre dirt, forest green, blue haze
shots.audio_cue: Continuous rock score and tire/air bed; landing accents from shared jump times.
continuity_dependencies: Same rider, bicycle, continuous increasing route distance
